clue.text: Punishment as part of learning

definitions.meaning: correction imposed to enforce rules, as in school or army
a branch of study, such as a field of academic knowledge

explanation.surface: A teacher's view that being punished is simply part of an education.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both enforced correction and a particular subject or branch of academic study.

clue.text: No good at making pudding

explanation.surface: Someone hopeless at making desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for worthless or faulty, and also a stodgy boiled dessert like plum duff.

clue.text: Sticks up for the self-satisfied

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the adjective, meaning pleased with oneself

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: Defending people who are pleased with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS into SMUG, read upward in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complacent people are excessively pleased with themselves.

clue.text: Introduced gradually in new list

indicators.note: new means the word list is rearranged into fresh form

explanation.surface: Something added little by little to a fresh list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LIST into STIL, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to implant an idea slowly, drop by drop, over time.

clue.text: It shows a sense of humour in trying circumstances

definitions.text: It shows a sense of humour in trying circumstances

parts.words: It shows a sense of humour in trying circumstances
parts.note: trying means difficult, but also a court trial, where amusement may break out

explanation.surface: A display of humour when things are tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement breaking out in a courtroom during a trial, often noted in reports.

clue.text: Standard a number considered average

definitions.meaning: a figure regarded as typical, like a usual reading

explanation.surface: A standard figure regarded as average.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ordinary or usual, and also describes a typical value.

clue.text: Smart bird with no tail

indicators.note: losing a tail means the last letter of the bird word is dropped

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

explanation.surface: A stylish bird that happens to lack a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone smart in appearance is elegant and stylish.

clue.text: Made bed in earth and wintered there

indicators.note: made, as in remade, says the letters are reassembled into something else

explanation.surface: An animal made its bed in the ground and spent the cold months there.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that spend winter dormant have passed the cold season asleep.

clue.text: Map soldiers employ to find a monastery

parts.note: a chart is a map
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to employ is to use

explanation.surface: Soldiers use a map to locate a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: La Grande Chartreuse is the mother house of the Carthusian monks near Grenoble.

clue.text: Sixteen standing firm

definitions.meaning: sixteen is four multiplied by itself, the second power of four

explanation.surface: A group of sixteen people holding their ground together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixteen is the square of four, and the phrase also means solid, steady and unflinching.

clue.text: Sailor goes to and fro in Arab garment

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: going there and back means the sailor's letters are given forwards and then backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor pacing back and forth wearing an Arab robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to and fro' gives AB forwards then backwards, BA.
explanation.definitionFit: An abba (or aba) is a loose sleeveless outer robe worn by Arabs.

clue.text: It comes before a fall

parts.note: echoes pride before a fall, but fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Echoes the proverb that pride goes before a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm season precedes autumn, which Americans call fall.

clue.text: Men on phone about an amazing spectacle

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Men on the telephone discussing something remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a remarkable or extraordinary sight or event.

clue.text: Where to find the colliery boss?

definitions.text: Where to find the colliery boss?

parts.words: Where to find the colliery boss?
parts.note: the boss of a coal mine would be its chief, but the clue really means the top of the mine shaft and its surface buildings

explanation.surface: Asking where the mine manager can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface works at the top of a mine shaft, read cryptically as the chief of the coal pit.

clue.text: Render first aid

definitions.meaning: to coat a wall with a layer, as a builder renders
a sticking dressing for a cut

explanation.surface: Give first aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to coat a wall with smooth mortar and also an adhesive dressing for a wound.

clue.text: Locked up as a final course

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tressed means having locks or tresses of hair

explanation.surface: Imprisoned for the last part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TRESSED (having locks of hair) backwards in this down entry. The surface makes 'Locked up' mean jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet dish served at the end of a meal is its last course.

clue.text: Describes a struggle of some gravity

definitions.text: Describes a struggle of some gravity

parts.words: Describes a struggle of some gravity
parts.note: a serious struggle, but literally one against gravity, as when climbing a slope

explanation.surface: A phrase describing a difficult and serious fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up a slope means working against gravity, so the word also means arduous.

clue.text: Acquired permit ran out inside

indicators.note: inside means the scrambled letters are placed within the word for permit

parts.note: to let is to permit or allow

indicators.note: out suggests the word ran is muddled or disordered

explanation.surface: Someone obtained a licence that expired while they were indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns RAN into ARN, and 'inside' places it within LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: knowledge acquired through study is knowledge gained.

clue.text: Senior politician in torment if seat is in jeopardy

indicators.note: something in jeopardy is under threat and disrupted, so these words get rearranged

explanation.surface: A government figure agonising because their parliamentary seat might be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK a minister of state is a senior government minister ranking just below cabinet level.

clue.text: Field marshal gains military medal in new role

indicators.note: gains means the anagram takes the medal letters into itself
new signals that the word role is rearranged into a fresh form

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A field marshal receives a decoration on taking up a different post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into ROEL; 'gains' puts MM inside it. Erwin Rommel was a German field marshal in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Rommel, the 'Desert Fox', held the rank of field marshal in the German army.

clue.text: Exceptional talent may be hidden

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the word talent is taken out of its usual order

explanation.surface: A remarkable gift may go unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dormant or concealed, present but not yet showing.

clue.text: Underwear sought by lawyers

definitions.meaning: barristers seek instructions on cases from solicitors

explanation.surface: Lawyers hunting for underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means short pants and also the case instructions a barrister receives.

clue.text: Human or not, they exist

parts.note: things that have existence, whether people or other creatures

explanation.surface: Living things, whether people or not.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing creatures or entities; people are called human ones.

clue.text: Idle chatter has teeth on edge

definitions.note: describes a toothed bar or wheel, a noun phrase read as 'thing which has teeth on its edge'

indicators.note: idle suggests the word chatter is loose and unsettled, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Pointless gossip that sets one's teeth on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teeth on edge' is an idiom for irritation, but here it describes a mechanism literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a wheel or bar with angled teeth along its rim, engaged by a pawl.

clue.text: Where various barmen work

parts.note: the workplaces of bar staff, plural pubs or taverns

explanation.surface: Asking where different bartenders are employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and hostelries are where people serving drinks are employed.

clue.text: I ask about the pen-name of H H Munro

definitions.text: the pen-name of H H Munro

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Asking about a writer's pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: H H Munro was an Edwardian British short-story writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Hugh Munro wrote his witty short stories under this pseudonym.

clue.text: Creatures having small feet with a point at each end

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
ft is the short form of feet
S, south, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Animals with little feet that are pointed at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point at each end' puts a compass point, E and S, either side of FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Efts are newts, small amphibians; creatures is the general term.

clue.text: Give 50% rebate on ticket?

parts.note: to give back half the price, but also the homeward portion of a two-way rail ticket

explanation.surface: A railway offering to refund half a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a two-way rail ticket used for the journey back home.

clue.text: Greek character bestriding N Italian mount

indicators.note: bestriding means straddling, so the Greek letter sits either side of N

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek person sitting astride a mountain in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the volcano in Sicily is the best-known mountain in Italy.

clue.text: They may be vital for beauty contestants

definitions.text: They may be vital for beauty contestants

parts.words: They may be vital for beauty contestants
parts.note: vital here means the phrase of bust, waist and hip measurements, not essential

explanation.surface: Something essential for people in a beauty pageant.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerical data; 'vital' ones are the bust, waist and hip measurements of a figure.
